records.contextBody: Rolex presents the Datejust family as a long-running design with a date display and multiple case, dial, bezel and bracelet combinations. records.imageMatchStatus: No exact-variant photograph is integrated. The separately labelled 126528LN Commons image is not used as this model’s image.
records.storyLead: Rolex introduced the Cosmograph Daytona in 1963 for motor-racing professionals. Its chronograph, three counters and tachymetric scale connect elapsed time with average speed.
records.storyBody: Rolex lists reference 126500LN as a 40 mm Cosmograph Daytona in Oystersteel. The model page describes calibre 4131, an approximately 72-hour power reserve and 100 m water resistance. No Venturo stock or price is represented.
records.galleryDescription: Exact-variant photography is unavailable here. The reference identifier links to the official Rolex model page; the family diagram is illustrative only.
records.galleryCaption: Rolex model reference; no product photograph is supplied for this variant.
records.featureBody1: The Rolex model page describes elapsed-time measurement through the central chronograph seconds hand, 30-minute counter and 12-hour counter.
records.featureBody2: The tachymetric bezel is used with elapsed time to read average speed over a measured distance. This description is attributed to Rolex.
records.featureBody3: Rolex identifies calibre 4131 as the self-winding mechanical chronograph movement for this reference family.
records.contextBody: Rolex’s Cosmograph Daytona story traces the family from its 1963 launch and its links to motor sport. The family identity, specifications and history on this page belong to Rolex; Venturo is presenting reference research only.
